sources.title: Zero-shot learning - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) is a problem setup in machine learning where, at test time, a learner observes samples from classes which were not observed during training, and needs to predict their class. The name is a play on words based on the earlier concept of one-shot learning in computer vision, in which classification can be learned from only one example. sources.title: What Is Zero-Shot Learning in AI? (2026 Guide)
sources.snippet: That's the basic intuition behind one of the more genuinely impressive capabilities in modern AI. So, what is zero-shot learning in AI, exactly? Zero-shot learning is the ability of a trained model to correctly handle a task, category, or example it never saw during training, with zero labeled examples provided for that specific case.
